questions.question_text: Under what condition is it legal to turn right on a red light in most of the United States?
options: You never have to stop at a red light
After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and traffic
Only if there is no other traffic in sight
At any time as long as you use your turn signal
questions.explanation: Turning right on red is permitted in all 50 states after a full stop and checking for safety, provided no signs prohibit it.

questions.question_text: What does the 'Move Over' law require you to do when passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane
Change lanes or slow down to provide space
Speed up to pass quickly and clear the area
Stop completely in the travel lane
questions.explanation: The Move Over law is designed to protect emergency responders and utility workers by requiring drivers to safely distance themselves from stopped vehicles with flashing lights.

questions.question_text: When approaching a four-way stop at the same time as another vehicle, who has the right of way?
options: The vehicle on the left
The vehicle that arrived first, or the vehicle on the right if arriving simultaneously
The vehicle that is going faster
The larger vehicle
questions.explanation: The basic rule at a four-way stop is that the person who reaches the intersection first goes first. If two people arrive at the same time, the person on the right has priority.

questions.question_text: What should you do when you see a vehicle entering a roundabout?
options: Accelerate to get in front of them
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout
Stop and wait for the roundabout to be empty
Enter immediately regardless of traffic
questions.explanation: Drivers entering a roundabout must yield to the vehicles already circulating inside it.

questions.question_text: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching from behind, what should you do?
options: Stay in your lane and maintain speed
Pull over to the right and stop if safe
Speed up to get out of the way
Make an immediate U-turn
questions.explanation: Drivers are required to pull over to the right side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

questions.question_text: At an uncontrolled intersection, who must yield?
options: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right
The driver going faster must yield
The driver going straight must yield to turning vehicles
Nobody has to yield
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question_text: If you arrive at a four-way stop at the same time as another vehicle, who has the right-of-way?
options: The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
The fastest vehicle
The larger vehicle
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two cars arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question_text: What must you do when approaching a roundabout?
options: Stop and wait for a green light
Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout
Always enter at high speed
Drive to the left of the center island
questions.explanation: Traffic inside the roundabout has the right-of-way; entering vehicles must yield to them.

questions.question_text: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should you do?
options: Always accelerate through
Yield to the vehicle on your right
Only yield to buses
Stop only if there is a sign
questions.explanation: At intersections without signs or signals, the general rule is to yield to the traffic approaching from the right.

questions.question_text: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching from behind, what is the safest action?
options: Stay in your lane
Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop
Increase your speed
Stop immediately in the middle of the road
questions.explanation: Drivers are required to pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles clear passage.
